solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: An A for apprenticeship

definitions.meaning: the words an and a are both indefinite ... in grammar
a trainee solicitor or accountant was formerly bound by ..., a training contract

explanation.walkthrough: Being 'articled' to a firm meant serving a formal apprenticeship there, a British usage for training as a solicitor or accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar calls a and an indefinite articles, and a training contract binding an apprentice clerk is also called articles.

clue.text: In disorder, arm staff that will press home a charge

definitions.text: that will press home a charge

indicators.note: in disorder says the letters of the next word are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: a staff is a rod or stick

explanation.surface: A soldier, arms in disarray, holds the staff used to load a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramrod is the rod used to push the charge down the barrel of a muzzle-loading gun.

clue.text: Does an evening job?

parts.note: evening here means making things even, smoothing creases out of clothes, not working at night

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a night shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening' looks like a time of day; it is the act of making even, which is what pressing laundry does.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes flat with a hot iron is literally making the fabric even.

clue.text: Cricket finalist?

parts.note: a finalist here is the final batsman of an innings, not a contender in a final

explanation.surface: A cricketer reaches the final of a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the eleventh batsman to come in to bat is called the last man in; 'finalist' is read as the final one.
explanation.definitionFit: The last batsman of a cricket side to go out to bat is the final one, the team's tailender.

clue.text: The foolish snipe at the wise

indicators.note: foolish means silly or muddled, telling us to jumble the letters that follow

explanation.surface: Silly people take a swipe at clever ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolish' rearranges SNIPE and AT together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient is a formal synonym for wise, showing deep knowledge and good judgement.

clue.text: Notice saying 'Playground equipment'

parts.note: to notice is to see
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: A sign reads 'Playground equipment'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plank pivoted in the middle, rocking children up and down, is a staple of playgrounds.

clue.text: People are unhappy when out of these groups

definitions.text: People are unhappy when out of these
definitions.meaning: to be out of ... is to feel unwell or grumpy
kinds or classes, groups of similar things

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom out of sorts means unhappy, and sorts also means categories or kinds.

clue.text: Risks of heat in terminals

indicators.note: in places the word for heat inside the word for terminals

parts.note: terminals are ends
heat is passion or anger

explanation.surface: Dangers of heat at the stations at each end of a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To risk something is to put it in danger, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Discharged sailor worked out

parts.note: AB is able seaman, a sailor
worked out means solved

explanation.surface: A seaman is released after his case is worked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolved means set free from blame or obligation, so released or discharged.

clue.text: Director's backing me first to do relief work

indicators.note: first says the turned piece comes ahead of the word for director
backing means turned back, so the word me is written right to left

parts.note: a director is a boss

explanation.surface: A manager's support puts me first in aid work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief work' suggests charity aid; here it is raised decoration. 'backing' turns the word me around, and 'first' places it ahead of the director.
explanation.definitionFit: Embossing is raising a design in relief on a surface, a pun on relief work as charity.

clue.text: Eden is in the march past

indicators.note: in says the word is goes inside the word for march past

parts.note: a march past is a parade
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Garden of Eden appears in a military procession.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is the biblical garden of Eden, the home of Adam and Eve.

clue.text: Clear course of action after study

indicators.note: after puts the course of action following the word for study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn
the Somme is a river, a course, which saw a great First World War battle, an action

explanation.surface: Clear plans are made after reading up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course of action' looks like a plan; it is the River Somme, scene of the 1916 battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Consommé is a thin clear soup, and clear is a common noun for such a soup.

clue.text: Observe nothing in being old and infirm

indicators.note: in puts the word for nothing inside the word for observe

parts.note: to observe is to see
nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A carer notices nothing wrong with an elderly patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Senile describes mental and physical decline from old age.

clue.text: Didn't remain wholly calm

parts.note: wholly hints at whole, so the phrase also describes something no longer in one piece

explanation.surface: Someone lost their composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wholly' sounds like 'whole': the idiom for losing composure also literally means breaking up.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pieces is an idiom for losing self-control, and literally for breaking apart.

clue.text: Treat wage adjusting as a political scandal

indicators.note: adjusting means changing the arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: Fiddling the pay rise is turned into a political scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nixon-era break-in and cover-up is the archetypal American political scandal.

clue.text: Walk recollected in Arden poem

indicators.note: recollected read as re-collected, gathered up again in a new order

explanation.surface: A stroll is remembered in a poem set in the Forest of Arden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like remembering; read as re-collected it means the letters are gathered up again in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade is a leisurely walk, or a paved walkway by the sea.

clue.text: Without notice, serviceman's in a pickle

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the serviceman's word goes around the notice

parts.note: a marine is a serviceman
an ad is a notice in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A soldier is in trouble because he got no warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here has its old sense of outside, not lacking, so the serviceman wraps around the notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A marinade is a seasoned liquid for soaking food, and pickle is a brine for preserving it.

clue.text: 'Ratty' making sure a knot can get undone

indicators.note: get undone means come apart, so these letters are untied and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grows irritable when the knot they tied comes loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British slang for bad-tempered, and cantankerous means irritable and quarrelsome.

clue.text: It's obvious I'd engaged in contest

indicators.note: engaged in means taking part inside, so the letters for I'd sit inside the word for contest

parts.note: an event is a contest
the contraction I'd written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Clearly I took part in the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means plain to see, a direct synonym of obvious.

clue.text: A piece of land away from home

parts.note: a field is a piece of land

explanation.surface: A plot of ground far from where one lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Afield means away from one's home or usual surroundings, as in far afield.

clue.text: It makes what's left look right

definitions.text: It makes what's left look right

parts.words: It makes what's left look right
parts.note: left and right here are sides, not wrong and correct, since a reflection swaps them

explanation.surface: Something that makes a wrong choice seem correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' reads as correct, but it is the direction: a reflection swaps left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: A looking glass reverses images, so the left side appears on the right.

clue.text: Give a telling-off to cook

definitions.meaning: to give someone a telling-off is to criticise them severely
to cook meat in an oven with dry heat

explanation.definitionFit: Roast means to cook in an oven and also, informally, to scold severely.

clue.text: Recognise who's who, yet I find that's mistaken

indicators.note: mistaken means wrongly ordered, so these letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: I keep confusing people's identities.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify people is to recognise them and tell who each one is.

clue.text: Trunk roots disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed means messed about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tree's base is unsettled when its underground parts are disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' and 'roots' suggest a tree, but the trunk here is the human body.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the human body, without head or limbs, is called the torso.

clue.text: Hard top makes vehicle fast

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
apace means quickly, fast

explanation.surface: A convertible's rigid roof makes the car quick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard top' suggests a car roof, but it is the shell of a tortoise or crab.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the hard upper shell of a turtle or crustacean.

clue.text: Didn't deny it's a selfish characteristic

parts.note: greed is a selfish trait

explanation.surface: Someone admits that greed is a selfish trait.
explanation.definitionFit: If you agreed with something you went along with it rather than denied it.

clue.text: Take exception to being ordered to leave again

parts.note: re is a prefix meaning again
sent means told to go

explanation.surface: Someone is offended at being dismissed a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter about it, to take offence at it.

clue.text: Toolshed adapted for climbers' requirements

indicators.note: adapted means changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden shed is converted to store mountaineering kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers need small footholds or grips in the rock to make progress.
